name: Compass Group PLC

listing.exchange: London Stock Exchange (FTSE 100) - ordinary shares traded in USD since 1-Apr-2026

corporate_actions.event: LSE trading currency of ordinary shares changed from GBp to USD (announced 5-Feb-2026, confirmed 18-Mar-2026). NOTE: brief said 'since Jan-2026' - verified effective date is 1-Apr-2026. LSE restated historic prices at fixed 1 GBp = 0.0132080 USD; Bloomberg used daily FX. Listing/FTSE inclusion unchanged; dividends still paid in GBP unless USD elected. Pipeline must divide by 1 (USD), not 100, for post-Apr-2026 prices.
Q3 FY26 trading update: organic +7.1%, NNB in 4-5% target range, retention 96%

geography.fx_notes: Underlying revenue by region FY24 ~68% North America / 23% Europe / 9% Rest of World (chart labels garbled in extract - INFERENCE on ordering). From FY25 Europe + RoW reported as 'International'; former RoW ~5% pro forma after exits. US INFERENCE ~62-65%. UK INFERENCE ~6-8%. No China.

kpis.name: Net new business
kpis.value: 4.5% FY25 (4.2% FY24); within 4-5% target in Q3 FY26

kpis.name: Mobilisation costs / wage pass-through
kpis.value: Mobilisation costs not quantified; pricing ~3% vs inflation (pass-through largely achieved per management)

company_fcf.definition: Underlying free cash flow (after capex, leases and interest; before M&A)

lease.source_id: IFRS filer; not extracted - data gap

acquisitions.notes: Bolt-ons in Europe (Hofmann's, CH&CO, Dupont Restauration, 4Service; Vermaat NL 2025 per recall, not verified this run); M&A guided to add ~2% profit growth FY26; exits from smaller RoW markets

management.guidance_record: Strong: FY26 guidance raised at H1 (operating profit growth >11% cc); organic consistently at/above guidance

guidance.value: Underlying operating profit growth >11% cc; organic revenue ~7%; ~2% profit growth from M&A; margin progression
Mid-to-high single-digit organic growth with profit growth ahead of revenue

evidence: Multi-year contracts across B&I, healthcare, education, sports & leisure, defence
A.rationale: Contracted with high retention; sports & leisure and B&I volumes have discretionary elements.

B.rationale: Purchasing scale and win rates differentiate.

evidence: Global #1 contract caterer; NA organic +9.1% vs Sodexo NA +2.8% FY25
C.rationale: Scale demonstrably converts into higher win/retention rates than peers.

evidence: First-time outsourcing ~half of new wins (management, recall)

E.rationale: US-heavy; just under the >70% single-country anchor.

evidence: Bolt-ons + buybacks; leverage ~1.3-1.5x company basis (provider incl. leases 2.1x)
G.rationale: Disciplined; larger European M&A now adds some integration risk.

evidence: Tech-campus B&I clients (hyperscalers) are food clients, not capex-linked
I2.rationale: Low; some exposure to tech employer headcount.

evidence: Mix of cost-plus/management-fee and P&L contracts; savings often shared
I4.rationale: Pass-through contracts limit retention of savings.

evidence: Inflation passed through 2022-25 with margin up

ai.notes: None; some B&I clients are tech companies (headcount, not capex).

gates.notes: Provider ND/EBITDA 2.1x (incl. leases). UK-listed but ~68% North America; UK consumer/travel well under 40%. FX: shares now USD-quoted on LSE - pipeline must not divide by 100 after 1-Apr-2026.

bull_points: Industry leader with 96% retention and 4-5% net new business driving ~7-9% organic growth.
Structural outsourcing runway and procurement scale (Foodbuy).
Asset-light, FCF $2.0bn and consistent guidance delivery.
bear_points: ~68% North America (US-concentrated) and exposure to sports & leisure/B&I volumes.
Thin 7.2% margins: wage inflation or contract mobilisation slippage hits profit quickly.
Pass-through contract structures limit retention of productivity gains; premium multiple vs peers.
thesis_breakers: Retention below 95% or NNB below 3% for a full year.
Underlying margin decline >30bp in a year.
